answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation down 6%, and two independent memories (memory_31, memory_86) converge on signup/onboarding simplification producing durable activation lift with no noted downside — this is the strongest, least risky lever under a single-experiment constraint. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but the same memory explicitly warns of -12% retention and that discounting masks underlying gaps rather than fixing them, which conflicts directly with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; using our one slot there would be reactive rather than value-preserving. Activation_messaging (memory_91) also addresses a live metric but onboarding simplification more directly targets the specific 4% completion drop and has two corroborating memories rather than one. I verify memory_31 and memory_86 before committing since they jointly justify the chosen action and were consolidated at different times, so confirming they describe consistent, non-conflicting original results reduces the risk of over-trusting a compressed summary. I deliberately keep scale small/guarded since underlying causes of the competitor-driven SMB pressure and the activation dip are not yet diagnosed, and a broad rollout could lock in an insufficient fix while masking the pricing threat.
